project.name: FLUX
project.summary: Tenant-neutral Rust, WebAssembly, and TypeScript JSON compression foundation for API payloads.
goals: Provide schema-aware JSON compression primitives for API communication.
Ship stable Rust, WebAssembly, and TypeScript package surfaces for the FLUX compression format.
Keep the compression core product-neutral, deterministic, benchmarkable, and independently releasable.
nonGoals: Own application transport policy, customer schemas, routing, authentication, billing, telemetry, or product-specific behavior.
Own organization-wide CI, release governance, or downstream deployment policy.
Embed sibling-project assumptions into the compression format or package APIs.

owns.name: flux-compression-format
owns.description: Frame format, schema inference, compression pipeline, delta encoding, and checksum behavior for FLUX payloads.

owns.name: flux-package-surfaces
owns.description: Rust crates, WebAssembly bindings, TypeScript package exports, examples, specifications, and benchmarks.

doesNotOwn: Application-specific API transport, routing, authentication, tenancy, billing, or telemetry.
Customer or sibling-project schemas beyond generic compression test fixtures.
Enterprise CI policy, organization rulesets, or downstream deployment workflows.

allowedDependencies.surface: project manifest schema, standards, and rollout audit

forbiddenCouplings: Do not couple compression behavior to any single product, customer, tenant, or API route.
Do not let application repositories import unpublished FLUX internals instead of package exports.
Do not change the frame format or package contract for one consumer without a spec or ADR update.

delivery.deployPath: npm packages @sylphx/flux + @sylphx/flux-wasm via .github/workflows/release.yml on main (OIDC trusted publishing and/or NPM_TOKEN).
delivery.productionProof: scripts/run-flux-differential.sh main-bound differential_green + npm registry readback (gitHead == publish commit) + install smoke (compress/decompress roundtrip).

gaps.description: Add repository CI for Rust tests, package builds, WASM builds, and benchmark smoke checks before full adoption.
Declare package and crate release paths plus the readback evidence required after publication.
Reconcile README install names and package repository metadata before treating package contracts as fully adopted.
